top.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
top.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Sven Ulreich not sure if he will retire after this season
top.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - MAY 6: Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer of FC Bayern München (R) and Goalkeeper Sven Ulreich of FC Bayern München look on ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 Semi Final Second Leg match between FC Bayern München and Paris Saint-Germain at Football Arena Munich on May 6, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich is currently operating under the impression that Manuel Neuer is going to retire after the end of this season, though they maintain that he is still the club’s number one keeper for the time being. He is currently out injured due to a partial tendon tear in his right foot sustained in Bayern’s win at Mainz earlier this month. While neither Neuer nor the club has said anything outright about what will happen after this season when his contract expires, the club has been preparing for life without him. The veteran keeper has been mentoring Jonas Urbig ever since the young keeper joined from FC Köln in the winter of 2025 for a fee of around €10 million. With Neuer’s injury history since Urbig arrived in Munich, the 23-year-old has gotten a considerable number of matches for the German Rekordmeister and has shown that he is ready to become the club’s number one keeper once Neuer is no longer in the pictu re. Both Julian Nagelsmann and Jürgen Klopp have even selected him for the senior Germany squad for recent international breaks, after he earned his first call-up in March of this year under Nagelsmann. For Urbig, the pathway is clear, and while what will happen with Neuer at the end of the season remains to be seen, retirement is looking like the most likely outcome. Even so, that still leaves the club with the question of what will happen with fellow veteran keeper Sven Ulreich. His contract is also set to expire this summer, and he hasn’t played a competitive match for Bayern since th e 1–1 draw with Bayer Leverkusen in the Bundesliga back in March. Prior to that game, he had gone over 500 days without a competitive appearance, largely because he had to take a substantial amount of time off for personal reasons. When asked whether he would be retiring with Neuer at the end of the season, Ulreich left the door open to all options. “I’m 38, Manuel is 40, so that’s a legitimate question. I will speak to FC Bayern in the near future about how things will proceed and what the club wants. I can’t speak on Manu’s behalf about what happens afte r the season, but I’m making everything dependent on him right now,” the veteran keeper explained (via @iMia SanMia ). When asked whether it was still conceivable that he would continue playing even if Neuer retires, Ulreich replied, “Anything is possible as long as I feel good, healthy, and fit. That’s currently the case. However, I’ve also learned that things can change quickly. I live in the here and now, and at the moment, I enjoy going out onto the pitch every day.” Bayern needs to hone in on what its plan will be.

top.title: Trading for Teoscar Hernandez is best for 2026 and beyond
top.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 12: Teoscar Hernández #37 of the Los Angeles Dodgers hits a sacrifice fly in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Phillies’ quest to solve their long-standing production issues in the outfield was thwarted somewhat when Japanese superstar Teruaki Sato signed a six-year, $120 million deal with the Chicago Cubs earlier this week. It had been hoped that the 27-year-old Triple Crown winner might become the first Japanese import to come directly from Japan to Philadelphia, but it was unsurprisingly not to be. Dave Dombrowski has acknowledged the Phillies need another everyday outfielder on the roster and, with Alec Bohm now a Kansas City Royal after signing a two-year, $20 million contract, they desperately need a productive right-handed bat in the middle of their lineup. Understandably, much of the attention has turned to 32-year-old veteran free agents Seiya Suzuki and Randy Arozarena. I’ve gone over the pros and cons of these two players in a previous post , and recent reports indicate Suzuki would prefer to play on the west coast, all things being equal. Seiya Suzuki is down to four teams, according to Sanspo Japan: Padres Blue Jays Phillies Mariners A source in the American baseball world revealed, "If the salary and contract terms were the same for multiple interested teams, he would choose the Padres." Another source said… pic.twitter.com/pCuI8QQug1 — Phillies Tailgate (@PhilsTailgate) November 27, 2026 I’d prefer Suzuki to Arozarena for the reasons I laid out in my article linked above. He is a more patient and consistent hitter and would bring a legitimate right-handed power to the middle of the Phils’ order. He also plays better defense than Arozarena, and all of the behind-the-numbers metrics indicate Arozarena’s otherworldly offensive performance a season ago may not be repeatable. All things being equal, signing Suzuki makes the most sense for 2027 and ‘28, but there is one other solution that could be wiser than committing at least $20 million a year for half a decade to a player well into their late-30s. The Los Angeles Dodgers are expected to make 34-year-old outfielder Teoscar Hernandez available in a trade this off-season. Whether that happens before or after the presumed lockout that will begin on December 2 is unknown. For a team like the Phillies, pursuing Hernandez in a trade rather than committing to Suzuki or Arozarena makes more sense from a long-term perspective. top.title: Colin and Mauleón: the Natalia duo who shook up Chivas Femenil's XI
top.description: Colin and Mauleón: the Natalia duo who shook up Chivas Femenil's XI With a few weeks left in the women’s league’s Apertura 2026, it is worth taking stock of how the season has gone for Chivas Femenil . The team is once again in the Liga Femenil Semifinals, finished second in Group B, and improved on several of its own benchmarks in the division, both in performance and results. Of course, this comes down to a collective effort, with quality in every area of the red-and-white squad, which has also strengthened in recent transfer windows. In the latest window, the club brought in 2 players who are now undisputed starters, have made a major impact on Antonio Contreras ’ system, and share a middle name. Natalia Colin and Natalia Mauleón arrived and broke into Guadalajara’s starting lineup, strengthening a team that already had a solid foundation but has continued to evolve thanks to both players’ contributions. Colin joined from Tigres, while Mauleón arrived from Pachuca with a clear aim: to add quality on the ball. Let’s start with Mauleón, who took part in the Rojiblanca Preseason and made her debut on Matchday 1 against Gallos, making a significant impact on the pitch. She changed the team’s dynamic through her distribution, pressing after losing possession, and chance creation, offering a taste of what she would deliver throughout the tournament. ‘Mau’ played all 16 league matches, averaging 81 minutes per game, providing 5 assists and recording 91% passing accuracy in the opposition half from midfield. For her part, Colin could not take part in the Rojiblanca Preseason because she was called up to the Mexican national team for the Central American and Caribbean Games, where she won gold with El Tri. But her eagerness to wear the colors of the Rebaño Sagrado was even greater: she flew from Santo Domingo to Puebla to make her first appearance for the team just days later. She came on as a substitute at Estadio Cuauhtémoc and has not relinquished her place in Guadalajara’s lineup since. At center back, Natalia has developed an excellent understanding with Cristina Ferral and Samantha López , strengthening the heart of the defense. She has even played as a holding midfielder, thanks to her reading of the game, anticipation, and vision on the ball, which allow her to win back possession and launch attacks for Chivas Femenil . She has made 15 appearances, played 1,298 minutes, and averaged 5 ball recoveries per match, alongside 88% passing accuracy in her own half. top.description: Reading haven’t been on the best form in recent times, with back-to-back losses glooming in the fans’ faces. Saturday November 28 brings football to Hillsborough. Kick-off is at 3pm and there’s a capacity of 39,814, so fill that stadium. Here are four of them: Joe Lumley is currently the starting goalkeeper with the Owls, where he has made 15 appearances so far this season. He has a save percentage of 76.5% and has made 31 saves. Will Keane played 13 matches for the Owls in 2014. That season he scored three goals and didn’t get an assist. He is on fire this season and could be the difference-maker this weekend. My predictions Joel Pereira will start in goal. Udoka Godwin-Malife, Paudie O’Connor, Benn Ward and Haydon Roberts will be the backline. Lewis Wing and Andy Rinomhota will be the defensive two. Leaving Daniel Kyerewaa, George Earthy and Josh Stokes to be the attacking midfielders. Marriott will of course be up top. Score prediction: 1-1 Good luck to those going to the game! top.title: Anthony Kim’s Return Is The Best Story In Modern Golf
top.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Anthony Kim is back, and he is not here to play small ball. The man who vanished for twelve and a half years just dropped the most honest interview in golf history. He spoke to Joe Rogan about his darkest days, his battle with addiction, and the family that pulled him out of the hole. GolfMagic reported that Kim opened up about a life he once struggled to imagine living. The numbers from his first tournament back look ugly to most fans. He finished 33 strokes behind the leader. That would have ended a normal career. Kim saw it differently. He told Rogan he was “so excited after that tournament” because he felt he could win the next week. His wife Emily believed him even when the rest of the world did not. He used the hate from online comments as fuel to practice longer. “When I say I’m done, I think about those comments and I stay out there for 30 minutes longer,” he said. The Turnaround Is Real That grit paid off in February 2026. Kim won LIV Golf Adelaide with a final-round nine-under-par 63. At the start of the day, he was five shots behind Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. He earned his first win in nearly 16 years by passing two of the sport’s most prominent figures. The crowd on the 18th green embraced the underdog story. Kim celebrated a three-shot victory that meant far more than a trophy. A New Kind of Player The old Anthony Kim was a fearless star who won three times before age 26. He was part of the winning 2008 Ryder Cup team. The new Anthony Kim is a 41-year-old father who prays for another day. He told Rogan that as a kid he prayed he would not wake up. “Now, when I wake up, I pray to God that I get one more day just so I could see that beautiful smile of my daughter and my wife who saved my life,” Kim said. His return to the winner’s circle is a rare feat in the modern game.

nigeria.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
nigeria.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nigeria set to bid to host maiden U-17 WAFCON
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria is preparing to bid to host the maiden edition of the Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), as the country seeks to attract more international sporting competitions and strengthen its sports economy. The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). According to Olopade, the country expressed its desire to host the competition during CAF’s General Assembly held in Abuja last weekend. “We have said to CAF that we are desirous of hosting the first Under-17 women’s championship,” he said. He explained that the move forms part of Nigeria’s ambition to move away from what he described as a consuming sports economy towards a productive one, where hosting international events would generate economic benefits for the country. “We don’t want to be a consuming sports economy; rather, we want to be a productive sports economy. We want to attract more international events where the economic impacts will be felt by the people,” Olopade added. CAF’s Executive Committee approved the introduction of the U-17 WAFCON on November 21, with the inaugural tournament scheduled to take place between March and April 2028. Qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027. Nigeria’s interest in hosting the competition comes amid discussions about the country’s readiness to stage major international football events. Earlier this week, FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Nigeria was not yet ready to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, although he acknowledged the country’s resources, passion and willingness to stage the competition. Infantino, however, suggested that Nigeria could demonstrate its organisational capacity by hosting smaller international football tournaments before taking on events of greater magnitude. The proposed U-17 WAFCON could therefore provide Nigeria with an opportunity to showcase its capacity to organise a continental football competition. nigeria.description: Hackers have breached Cloud One, the United States Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially exposing sensitive military, personnel and logistics data. Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the intrusion was discovered within the past month during efforts to upgrade the system, triggering disruptions across the platform. However, the identity of the hackers, the full extent of the breach and whether any data was stolen remain unknown. In a statement to Reuters, the US Air Force declined to discuss the security status of specific networks and systems. It said: “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.” A major military computing platform Launched in 2017, Cloud One was designed as a centralised platform for the Air Force’s information technology needs, bringing together services provided by four major technology companies: Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. The platform supports dozens of applications, including systems managing personnel records, salaries, logistics and military equipment maintenance. Among the applications hosted on Cloud One are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control system, which consolidates air defence radar and other data feeds across North America, and the Theatre Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 US Air Force locations worldwide. Investigators have reportedly involved US Cyber Command, the military’s cyber warfare arm, to assess the damage. Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) served as the platform’s prime contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over the contract. SAIC did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment, while Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. nigeria.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
nigeria.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing interest in contesting the elections. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. History is not kind to breaks like that. entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. Things Fall Apart (1987) Before Nollywood’s home-video boom even began, Pete Edochie became a household name across Nigeria and internationally through his breakout role as Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel Things Fall Apart. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Sven Ulreich not sure if he will retire after this season
sports.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - MAY 6: Goalkeeper Manuel Neuer of FC Bayern München (R) and Goalkeeper Sven Ulreich of FC Bayern München look on ahead of the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 Semi Final Second Leg match between FC Bayern München and Paris Saint-Germain at Football Arena Munich on May 6, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich is currently operating under the impression that Manuel Neuer is going to retire after the end of this season, though they maintain that he is still the club’s number one keeper for the time being. He is currently out injured due to a partial tendon tear in his right foot sustained in Bayern’s win at Mainz earlier this month. While neither Neuer nor the club has said anything outright about what will happen after this season when his contract expires, the club has been preparing for life without him. The veteran keeper has been mentoring Jonas Urbig ever since the young keeper joined from FC Köln in the winter of 2025 for a fee of around €10 million. With Neuer’s injury history since Urbig arrived in Munich, the 23-year-old has gotten a considerable number of matches for the German Rekordmeister and has shown that he is ready to become the club’s number one keeper once Neuer is no longer in the pictu re. Both Julian Nagelsmann and Jürgen Klopp have even selected him for the senior Germany squad for recent international breaks, after he earned his first call-up in March of this year under Nagelsmann. For Urbig, the pathway is clear, and while what will happen with Neuer at the end of the season remains to be seen, retirement is looking like the most likely outcome. Even so, that still leaves the club with the question of what will happen with fellow veteran keeper Sven Ulreich. His contract is also set to expire this summer, and he hasn’t played a competitive match for Bayern since th e 1–1 draw with Bayer Leverkusen in the Bundesliga back in March. Prior to that game, he had gone over 500 days without a competitive appearance, largely because he had to take a substantial amount of time off for personal reasons. When asked whether he would be retiring with Neuer at the end of the season, Ulreich left the door open to all options. “I’m 38, Manuel is 40, so that’s a legitimate question. I will speak to FC Bayern in the near future about how things will proceed and what the club wants. I can’t speak on Manu’s behalf about what happens afte r the season, but I’m making everything dependent on him right now,” the veteran keeper explained (via @iMia SanMia ). When asked whether it was still conceivable that he would continue playing even if Neuer retires, Ulreich replied, “Anything is possible as long as I feel good, healthy, and fit. That’s currently the case. However, I’ve also learned that things can change quickly. I live in the here and now, and at the moment, I enjoy going out onto the pitch every day.” Bayern needs to hone in on what its plan will be.

Yup. #Blackhawks have placed Patrick Kane on injured reserve with a lower-body injury, retroactive to Nov. 25. Landon Slaggert has been recalled from Rockford. Kane will miss at least the next 3 games. He’s eligible to return next Thursday in Nashville. pic.twitter.com/Hu5BuLhgba — Jack Bushman (@JackBushman2) November 27, 2026 Kane exited Wednesday’s 3-1 win over the Seattle Kraken late in the third period after blocking a shot with his right leg/foot in the defensive zone. The 38-year-old veteran gingerly skated off the ice and went immediately into the locker room. Kane didn’t return for the final 3:01, and he’ll now miss at least the next three games. #Blackhawks officially place Patrick Kane (lower body) on injured reserve retroactive to Nov. 25. He blocked a shot off his right foot/ankle at the end of the game on Wednesday. pic.twitter.com/Dw1nMu87GF — Charlie Roumeliotis (@CRoumeliotis) November 27, 2026 Per NHL guidelines, Kane must remain on injured reserve for a minimum of seven days, meaning he’s eligible to return next Thursday against the Nashville Predators. Kane will not play on Black Friday against the New York Rangers, and he’ll also miss the upcoming back-to-back on Monday and Tuesday against Minnesota and Winnipeg. The development is another crushing blow to the Blackhawks, as Kane had been playing his best hockey of the season since returning from a three-game absence earlier this month. Before exiting Wednesday’s win, Kane extended his point streak to six games with an assist on Roman Kantserov ‘s game-winning goal. During his point streak, Kane had recorded nine points, including his first goal since opening night on Sept. 30. In last Saturday’s 4-3 overtime win over the Calgary Flames , Kane recorded his first three-point outing of the season and snapped his career-long 18-game goal drought. Kane had been much more involved offensively recently, and his playmaking was a huge part of the turnaround from the top power-play unit, which has also scored in six straight games and gone 11-for-20 during that stretch. At even strength, Kane’s line with Frank Nazar and Oliver Moore has also been the best and most consistent trio for head coach Jeff Blashill in the last few weeks. Kane’s absence will be felt on the power play and at 5-on-5. With Kane on injured reserve, the Blackhawks recalled winger Landon Slaggert from the Rockford IceHogs. The 24-year-old has yet to play an NHL game this season but appeared in 53 games for the Blackhawks in 2025-26, tallying three goals and four assists for seven points. sports.title: Nico Paz will only consider Real Madrid return under one condition
sports.description: Nico Paz will only consider Real Madrid return under one condition Como star Nico Paz has made clear that he would only even take into consideration a return to former employers Real Madrid under one strict condition. This of course comes amid the ongoing speculation linking the Argentine with a move back to Spain’s capital next summer. After agreeing to remove their cut-price buy-back clause for Paz in exchange for a €60 million permanent deal with Como earlier this year, the Santiago Bernabéu brass will have the opportunity to bring their ex-midfield prodigy back to Valdebebas once again upon this season’s close. This would require a sum of €80 million. Paz’s excellence over the early months of the new campaign, though, has already given rise to claims that Florentino Pérez would be prepared to fork over such a sum. The final say, though, will be with the midfielder himself. And if the latest word stemming from the media late this week is anything to go by, then Real Madrid could face a tough battle in convincing Paz of the merits of a comeback. As per a report from The Athletic : ‘Sources privy to the matter, talking anonymously to protect relationships, suggest Paz does not currently favour rejoining Madrid. This stance might alter if he is assured of a prominent role — that has not been the case.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

sports.title: Anthony Kim’s Return Is The Best Story In Modern Golf
sports.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Anthony Kim is back, and he is not here to play small ball. The man who vanished for twelve and a half years just dropped the most honest interview in golf history. He spoke to Joe Rogan about his darkest days, his battle with addiction, and the family that pulled him out of the hole. GolfMagic reported that Kim opened up about a life he once struggled to imagine living. The numbers from his first tournament back look ugly to most fans. He finished 33 strokes behind the leader. That would have ended a normal career. Kim saw it differently. He told Rogan he was “so excited after that tournament” because he felt he could win the next week. His wife Emily believed him even when the rest of the world did not. He used the hate from online comments as fuel to practice longer. “When I say I’m done, I think about those comments and I stay out there for 30 minutes longer,” he said. The Turnaround Is Real That grit paid off in February 2026. Kim won LIV Golf Adelaide with a final-round nine-under-par 63. At the start of the day, he was five shots behind Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. He earned his first win in nearly 16 years by passing two of the sport’s most prominent figures. The crowd on the 18th green embraced the underdog story. Kim celebrated a three-shot victory that meant far more than a trophy. A New Kind of Player The old Anthony Kim was a fearless star who won three times before age 26. He was part of the winning 2008 Ryder Cup team. The new Anthony Kim is a 41-year-old father who prays for another day. He told Rogan that as a kid he prayed he would not wake up. “Now, when I wake up, I pray to God that I get one more day just so I could see that beautiful smile of my daughter and my wife who saved my life,” Kim said. His return to the winner’s circle is a rare feat in the modern game.

sports.title: May’s Mavs Roster Depth Is A True Feast For Dallas Fans
sports.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Dallas coach Dusty May does not need a turkey dinner to feel thankful. He looked at his team on the court and saw a deep bench full of proven stars. The Mavericks are riding a four-game winning streak into Friday night. They are 11-7 before facing the Phoenix Suns. This success came as a surprise to many who predicted a rougher season for the team. A Roster Built For Sacrifice May sees more than ten players who have started games for other NBA teams. He told reporters he is “Very grateful for our roster and the team that has been put together,” per NBA.com . The coach noted that his players cheer for each other with no envy in the locker room. Role definitions have grown on their own because the guys know what they need to do. May admitted that after big wins, he almost feels bad that certain players did not get enough minutes. Max Christie and Santi Aldama are key parts of this depth but sit on the bench often. A year ago, Christie was perhaps the second-best player during the first half of the season. He knows his job is to stay ready even when he isn’t on the field. “One of the most important things as an NBA player is to stay ready,” Christie said. He said the team includes experienced players who have logged significant minutes previously. The guys waiting to play work hard behind the scenes so they are ready when called. Young Sparks And A Key Absence Zaccharie Risacher, Caleb Martin, Daniel Gafford, Naji Marshall, and P.J. Washington have propelled this run through their performance. This group has taken pressure off Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. Rookie Morez Johnson Jr. and two-way signee Walter Clayton Jr. have also supplied sparks as their roles grew. But the biggest story might be the player who has not played yet this season. Dereck Lively II has been on the three-game trip and provides an uplifting story for the team. May said, “I couldn’t be more grateful (for Lively),” according to NBA.com. His consistency and care for teammates make him the ultimate teammate, even from the bench.

sports.title: 'Hopefully I can stay for many more years' - Martin Odegaard confident over new Arsenal contract ahead of Manchester City showdown
sports.description: Odegaard Napoli Arsenal Martin Odegaard has insisted he is not worried about his Arsenal contract and hopes to stay at the club for many more years. The captain's current deal runs until 2028, but he is confident new terms will be agreed as the Premier League champions continue to tie down their key players, with Mikel Arteta's side preparing to host Manchester City on Sunday. Odegaard relaxed over contract future Arsenal are tying down the likes of Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie to new long-term contracts, and Odegaard has told Sky Sports News he expects to follow suit, with his current deal set to expire in 2028. "It's not something I stress about," Odegaard said. "I've said it so many times, I'm so happy here, I love it here. Hopefully I can stay for many more years - and I think the club is happy as well. So it's no stress, we'll sort it out." Captain wants to 'win everything' Odegaard, who has been linked with Bayern Munich, said while on international duty with Norway earlier this month that he hoped to stay at Arsenal "for a long time", but admitted talks over a new deal had not started yet. "The main thing is to focus on the pitch, and then we'll see what happens," he added. "I want to win more things here for sure. I want to win everything with Arsenal. The Premier League again, the Champions League, the cups - that's what we want. We want to win everything." 'We have everything here' The 27-year-old insisted the team comes first. "The rest of it, the individual stuff, will come as a result of what happens with the team. The team is the most important bit," he said. Odegaard also believes Arsenal have all the ingredients to go again: "We have everything we need. We have shown we can do it, now it's time to show we can do it again, to win even more and take another step. We have everything here, coaching staff, amazing squad, amazing players and people." Arsenal prepare for Man City showdown Odegaard and Arsenal now turn their attention to Sunday's visit of Manchester City , with the Premier League leaders six points ahead of Enzo Maresca's side. Victory would move the Gunners nine points clear of City, although they remain without Bukayo Saka, who is set to be out for another three weeks.

sports.title: Colts HC Sends Clear Message to Anthony Richardson Before Start
sports.description: The Indianapolis Colts are making their final preparations for Week 12 action on Sunday afternoon against the New York Giants at home. In that game, the team will get its first look at its new starting quarterback. Former No. 4 overall pick Anthony Richardson is the Colts’ new starter. After the team opted to release Daniel Jones, Richardson will be given another opportunity to show that he can be a long-term fit for Indianapolis. So far since being the No. 4 pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, Richardson has played in just 19 total games. He has completed 50.6 percent of his career pass attempts for 2,408 yards, 11 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions, while also running for 640 yards and 10 more touchdowns. Ahead of this week’s game against the Giants, head coach Shane Steichen spoke out with a clear message to his new starting quarterback. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. (5) takes the field to face the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Colts’ Shane Steichen Has Clear Message for Anthony Richardson As shared by Colts beat writer James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen knows that Richardson will bring splash plays to the table. He wants to see development in another area of the young signal caller’s game. “We all know he’s gonna make the splash plays,” Steichen said . “We’re excited to see that. But just taking the easy completions, and he’s improved on that as his career has went on.” Richardson has struggled to make the easy plays throughout his young career. Those struggles have been a big part of the reason for the 50.9 career completion percentage. Needless to say, a change was necessary for Indianapolis. At this point in the year, the Colts have a 3-8 record. They already shipped out quite a few key players before the trade deadline, including offensive lineman Quenton Nelson, wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Hopefully, Richardson can come out against New York and have a strong game. He has a short runway to prove that he deserves to be re-signed by the Colts during the offseason. sports.title: Decline of deities - the long game the All Blacks cannot afford to lose
sports.description: Codie Taylor led the New Zealand haka against England before the 37-12 defeat last Saturday [Getty Images] For decades, the All Blacks have defied gravity. Despite a population, player pool and bank balance smaller than most of their rivals, New Zealand's rugby team have become sporting shorthand for success. Deservedly so. No other team comes close to them. England beat the All Blacks this year and last. They play them again on Saturday aiming for a hat-trick. But, England would need that winning streak to continue until around 2050 just to level up a lop-sided historical head-to-head. New Zealand have won 36 times to England's 10 in their 121-year rivalry. For every other nation in Test rugby, the story is the same. New Zealand have the superior record against them all. A section on the All Blacks' website, titled Rivalries, opens by listing South Africa's 40% winning record in their meetings. And the numbers only drop from there. But New Zealand's grip on the global game appears looser now than ever. If they lose to England on Saturday, it may not much sway the historical balance between the two teams. But it would be a sixth defeat in a calendar year, a total matched only once before in the All Blacks past, back in 1949 when a split squad played two Test series in Australia and apartheid South Africa at the same time. New Zealand's win percentage in 2026 is 58.3%, their third lowest for any year since the start of professionalism. This campaign, marked by an exhausting schedule and four Tests away to the world champion Springboks, is in keeping with a recent trend. Since the end of the 2010s - a period in which an all-time great team captured back-to-back world titles - New Zealand have come off the boil. The 2020s are on course to be their least successful decade since the 1970s. This current crop of All Blacks are suffering not just by comparison to the previous generation, but when set against every other modern predecessor. One reason may be a source of strength turning against them. The All Blacks' culture of promoting within and establishing coaching dynasties was seen as key when they were winning. A thread ran through the Graham Henry, Steve Hansen and Ian Foster succession in the 2010s glory days. The latter two served under their predecessor and the first two earned their Test stripes with Wales, before taking the top job. All were schooled as coaches in New Zealand and steeped in the country's rugby traditions. The in-house production line of leaders ensured continuity and protected a team ethos that has been admired and written about everywhere. But, in a modern world in which opposition tactics are quickly picked apart and best practice spreads fast, has adherence to tradition held back the team? sports.title: 3 reasons why Alabama will defeat Auburn in Iron Bowl, 3 why not
sports.description: Every time Alabama and Auburn get together it is a big game, and once again, this year's Iron Bowl also has a lot at stake. Alabama (9-2 overall, 6-2 SEC) is looking to lock up their spot in the College Football Playoff (CFP), while Auburn (7-4, 4-4) is looking to keep up their momentum under first-year head coach Alex Golesh and to wrap up the regular season in the top 25. For Alabama, a win would fully lock them into the CFP, as well as potentially the SEC championship game depending on what happens elsewhere, while a loss would mean some sweating over the next week with them on the bubble heading into Selection Sunday. Auburn meanwhile has won three-straight and has some momentum going as they are looking to surge into the top 25 with a late-season run in the first season of a new era. What could decide the winner of this Iron Bowl? Well, here are three reasons why Alabama will win, as well as three reasons they might not. Why: Alabama's pass rush against Auburn's offensive line One of the biggest areas of weakness this season for Auburn has been allowing sacks. Auburn is bottom five nationally and tied for worst in the SEC having allowed 39 sacks this season. That's just over 3.5 per game. On the flip-side, Alabama's defense ranks in the top 25 nationally in producing sacks this year with 31. Now, not all of Auburn's sacks allowed is on the offensive line. There have been issues this season with Byrum Brown holding the ball too long. But, whichever the case, this is an opportunity for Alabama's pass rush to have a big day, although they will have to stay disciplined. Why Not: Auburn's pass rush against Alabama's offensive line There's a similar story, not as extreme though, on the flip-side. Alabama's offensive line ranks just outside the top 100 nationally in sacks allowed with 28. Auburn's pass rush has been slightly better than Alabama's at getting to the quarterback this season with 33 sacks, tied for tenth-most nationally. If Auburn is going to slow down Alabama's passing attack, one way to do it will to be to get after the quarterback. Why: Success to be had against Auburn's defense Auburn's defense has disappointed at times this season. It was a hyped-up unit in the offseason after retaining DJ Durkin as defensive coordinator, but the Tigers defense has struggled at times this season. Auburn's defense is middle of the pack in the SEC in scoring defense, allowing 23.9 points per game. However, it is bottom three in the SEC in yards allowed, passing yards allowed, and rushing yards allowed per game. Auburn is also outside the top 60 nationally in third down defense, and in their losses is when those issues have really shown up. In Auburn's four losses they are allowing 37.8 points per game. In their four SEC wins, Auburn is allowing 17.8 points per game. While it's obvious to say "they generally lose when they allow more points," that is a pathway for Alabama to win the game with their very talented offense led by a superstar quarterback

sports.title: Mercedes set pace in eventful Qatar second practice
sports.description: Gasly hit an advertising board after leaving the track [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix. Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session. Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid. The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes. The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin. Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs. The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions. "It was a productive day," said Antonelli. "We tried a lot of things on the car between FP1 and FP2, but in FP2, it seemed like we did a step back with the car. "But it was very interesting to see how the car behaved after those changes. It's not easy." Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them. He said he feels it will be close between himself and Russell for the race victory, but added: "You can never write off Max [Verstappen] and the others." Norris, meanwhile, said Mercedes "were in a different category" to McLaren, highlighting the Silver Arrows "were quicker in every single corner by miles". The 2025 world champion added: "We seem in a relatively decent position, similar on pace with Red Bull, and similar-ish to Ferrari. So I'd say it's OK." Four-time title winner Verstappen said it had been a "difficult day" following his issues with heavy steering towards the end of the session. "The balance of the car is probably too disconnected at the moment to go fast," he added. "It's costing us quite a bit of lap time." Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run. Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed. The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was sixth on the timesheets, with Leclerc leading Hamilton in seventh and eighth, 1.3 seconds away from Antonelli's time. technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®
